analysis.title: DB CoTD: A Strait Choice: $74 or $130
key_insights: DB's Energy analyst Michael Hsueh sees Brent at either $74 or $130 in 2027, depending on whether the Middle East war ends or drags on through next year. The gap between the two outcomes is $56.
Vessel attacks in the Middle East rose in October to their highest since the war began, and IMO-confirmed incidents may double this month.
Crude exports had run close to normal rates thanks to the US blockade and shuttle system. The volume leaving the region is now down from its late-September peak.
Arabian Gulf to Mediterranean VLCC charter rates have doubled from $16 to $32/bbl.
Brent is around $110, above DB's Q4 adverse scenario of $105 and the $95 base case.
The oil market went from a 1.7mb/d surplus in 2025 to a 1.8mb/d deficit this year. If Hormuz flows normalise, Hsueh sees a 4.1mb/d surplus in 2027.
Hsueh's base case is a negotiated ceasefire leading to broader talks, with Brent falling to $74 in 2027, about a third below today's level.

Brent dropped $6 in a few hours yesterday on headlines that Qatar and Pakistan had put forward a proposal that could revive talks. Oil then rallied again after a diplomat involved in negotiations said reports of a near-deal were false, though talks are ongoing.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Spot is above DB's Q4 adverse scenario ($105) and base case ($95), so the market is pricing a worse outcome than DB's own scenarios.
DB's base case for Q4 is $15 below spot.
Spot at $110 is already above this scenario.
A negotiated ceasefire leading to broader talks takes Brent about a third below today's level.
If the war continues through next year, Brent heads toward $130.
The market moved from a 1.7mb/d surplus in 2025 to a deficit this year.
The surplus appears if Hormuz flows normalise, which would put downward pressure on prices.

macro_indicators.indicator: Arabian Gulf to Med VLCC charter rate
macro_indicators.interpretation: Rates doubled from $16/bbl, showing higher shipping costs from the disruption.

risk_factors: Escalating vessel attacks in the Middle East could cut crude exports further.
A war lasting through 2027 would push Brent toward $130.
Headline-driven swings, such as a $6 move in Brent within hours, can reverse quickly when reports are denied.
geopolitical: Middle East war: vessel attacks in October are the highest since the war began.
US blockade and shuttle system kept crude exports near normal rates, but volumes leaving the region are now below the late-September peak.
Strait of Hormuz flows are central to the 2027 oil outlook.
Qatar and Pakistan reportedly put forward a proposal that could revive talks to end the conflict. A diplomat involved in negotiations said reports that the sides were close to a solution were false.
